steps.prompt: Which word do we use for more than one person or thing?
steps.why: One thing takes was. Two or more take were.
steps.html:
The team was from Jamaica.

There was no ice.

They were very popular.

There were no bobsleighs.

steps.title: was / were
steps.html:
PersonPositiveNegative
II was at home.I wasn't at home.
He / She / ItShe was a student.She wasn't a student.
You / We / TheyThey were happy.They weren't happy.

was and were are the past of am, is and are.

Use was after I, he, she and it. Use were after you, we and they.

For the negative, add n't: wasn't, weren't.

Learners often say I were. After I it is always was.

Other past verbs come in Lesson 2.

steps.title: Listen to the questions and the short answers.

items.text: Was it easy for them to practise? — No, it wasn't.
Were there bobsleighs for them to use? — No, there weren't.

steps.title: Questions and short answers
steps.html:
QuestionYesNo
Was it easy?Yes, it was.No, it wasn't.
Were you at home?Yes, I was.No, I wasn't.
Were they happy?Yes, they were.No, they weren't.

For a question, put was or were before the person: Were you at school?

Short answers do not repeat everything: Yes, I was. — not Yes, I was at school.

Wh- questions work the same way: Where were you born?
